title: the DSG Deepearth areas 4-5

banner.title: THE DSG DEEPEARTH AREAS 4-5, R535: printed pp. 79-81 (pdf 80-82) - the individual area key continues with the middle pair of areas: Area 4 Cathedral Caverns (the four great limestone caverns ranging 1d6 miles in length with ceilings up to 100 ft and a few 80- and 90-ft-wide spots, the stalactite-stalagmite-drapery abundance giving the ornately decorated cathedral appearance; the west tunnel rising to the surface and the ancient excavated connecting tunnel to the vast many-leveled dungeon below the surface city, its single Deepearth route concealed by a secret door; the 400-ft sinkhole from the forest above with the bandit escape route, the cave-in rubble and the secret-door notice; the clean cold water of the shallow narrow streams, five feet wide and one foot deep; the isolated pocket of hostile drow - about 25 fighters and an equal number of noncombatants, poor and far from their homeland's potent magic; the piercer-lined cathedral ceiling with the drow's faint rim trail; the jellies and oozes, the rats-giant rats-wererats of the city tunnel, and the otyugh and neo-otyugh scavengers; the 12-HD hydra fallen down the sinkhole, starving and nearly berserk; the diamond-vein cul-de-sac settled by jewelry proficiency; the scarce food with the drow stockpiling; the 500-ft drow approach tunnel under 10 ft wide - pit traps, 6d6 falling blocks, shriekers, an illusionary dead end, the steep last 100 ft with oil pots and archer niches; and the geothermal mud pool with its gold dust - 20 gp per coated character, more than 10,000 gp in all, 20 ft wide and 5 ft deep), and Area 5 Enclosed Caverns (the air-filled natural caves whose only entrance and exit are completely water-choked, fed by the subterranean river from the south-shore cave of the great lake; the 3-to-4 meander with the upstream sandy beach; the rapids a mile before the area and the cascade with no airspace that sweeps masts and tillers 80% of the time before the two-round tumble into the quiet pool of the vast entry cavern; the eight connected caves, each under a mile, joined by tunnels less than two feet in diameter; the far-end chute - the water-filled plunge of 50 ft, then less than a foot of clearance for about six miles to the long waterfall of Area 14; the pathetic mad castaways of a dozen expeditions, about 20 mostly men with their green-glowing fungi light; the kuo-toa outpost of 6d6 fish-men guarding the chute with their monthly sweeps, their downstream slave escorts and their insane wanderers; the fish, rats, beavers, weasels, rabbits and the occasional freshwater scrag; the nereid of the deep riverside-spring pool; the foam-assured air, the limited fungi, the plentiful netted fish; the 1%-per-hour river-bottom finds - plate mail +2, shield +2, shield +3, longsword +1, spear +3; the surface net stopping several feet short of the bottom; and the outpost's three vertical levels, secret doors and elaborate food-storage chamber)
banner.provenance: the DSG scan (archive.org item advanced-dungeons-dragons-1st-edition), pdf = printed + 1; the text read from the IA djvu OCR (djvu.txt lines ~10084-10295) with the pdf Acrobat-Capture layer as the second read (idx 368-372 = the printed pp. 79-81 windows); the compiled-tables appendix has no reprint of this prose. A CLEAN-READ ROUND: both machine reads agree on every load-bearing number - the four 1d6-mile caverns, the 100-ft ceilings, the 80/90-ft widths, the 400-ft sinkhole, the 5-ft-wide 1-ft-deep streams, the 25 drow fighters, the 12-HD hydra, the 500-ft tunnel under 10 ft wide with its 6d6 blocks and 100-ft climb, the mud pool's 20/5-ft size with the 20-gp and 10,000-gp gold, the 3-to-4 river rate, the one-mile rapids, the 80% sweep, the two cascade rounds, the eight sub-mile caves with the 2-ft tunnels, the 50-ft water-filled plunge and the six low-clearance miles, the 20 castaways, the 6d6 kuo-toa, the 1% finds and the outpost's three levels; the only garbles are non-load-bearing (the djvu 'GPPER' header noise, its Cyrillic glyph substitutions, and the Capture 'ievel' and 'kua-toa' spellings). SEAMS: the R518 water travel (the river flow rates and the cascade), the Monster Manual denizens (the drow, piercers, hydra, otyughs, kuo-toa, nereid, scrag and the rest), the R503 re-grain. A ZERO-FLIP ROUND: the pp. 75-98 Deepearth child remains open until the setting lands in full (the R527/R533/R534 precedent - the gap report is NOT in the git add). Nothing auto-credits.
banner.sentinel: A procedural-plus-prose round: no tables pin. The numbers pin as consts per the R508 convention - the cavern dimensions and stream sizes, the sinkhole depth, the drow lair and tunnel numbers, the mud pool's gold, the river rates and cascade odds, the cave-chain and chute numbers, and the castaway, kuo-toa and outpost counts, with the 1d6/6d6/6d6 dice pinned as count-and-sides const pairs. The geography, denizens, resources and unique-features prose pins as bools for both areas. The R518/MM/R503 seams are noted; the Deepearth child stays open; nothing auto-credits.

consts.name: dnacCavernCount
consts.comment: the region is made up of several very large limestone caves; four caverns run the length of the area, connected by narrower passages with a number of side passages.

consts.name: dnacCavernLenDice
consts.comment: each of the four great caverns ranges in length from 1d6 miles (the die count).

consts.name: dnacCavernLenSides
consts.comment: each of the four great caverns ranges in length from 1d6 miles (the die sides).

consts.name: dnacCeilingMaxFt
consts.comment: each large cavern has a ceiling that ranges up to 100 feet high in places.

consts.name: dnacWideLowFt
consts.comment: each cavern has a few locations where it is 80 or 90 feet wide (the low bound).

consts.name: dnacWideHighFt
consts.comment: each cavern has a few locations where it is 80 or 90 feet wide (the high bound).

consts.name: dnacSinkholeDepthFt
consts.comment: a side passage off the central cavern is pierced by a sinkhole from the surface that plunges 400 feet to the cavern floor, used as an escape route by bandits living in the forest above.

consts.name: dnacStreamWidthFt
consts.comment: the water flowing through these caverns is clean and cold; the streams tend to be about five feet wide.

consts.name: dnacStreamDepthFt
consts.comment: most of the water flows down shallow, narrow stream beds about one foot deep, with a few still, deep pools scattered about.

consts.name: dnacDrowFighters
consts.comment: an isolated pocket of drow lairs in one side cavern; the band numbers about 25 fighters and an equal number of noncombatants.

consts.name: dnacHydraHD
consts.comment: a 12 Hit Dice hydra fell down the sinkhole some years back, survived, forced its way into the central cavern, and has somehow managed to survive there - constantly hungry and nearly berserk with frustration.

consts.name: dnacTunnelLenFt
consts.comment: the only approach to the drow cavern is through a 500-foot-long tunnel.

consts.name: dnacTunnelMaxWidthFt
consts.comment: the drow approach tunnel is less than 10 feet wide along its entire length.

consts.name: dnacTunnelClimbFt
consts.comment: the last 100 feet of the drow approach tunnel climb steeply, where the drow have pots of oil ready to pour down upon intruders.

consts.name: dnacTrapDice
consts.comment: precariously balanced blocks of stone fall on trespassers who trip camouflaged releases, dealing 6d6 damage (the die count).

consts.name: dnacTrapSides
consts.comment: precariously balanced blocks of stone fall on trespassers who trip camouflaged releases, dealing 6d6 damage (the die sides).

consts.name: dnacMudPoolWidthFt
consts.comment: a corner of one of the small side caverns holds a bubbling pool of thick geothermally heated mud, about 20 feet wide.

consts.name: dnacMudPoolDepthFt
consts.comment: the geothermal mud pool is about five feet deep, very warm but not dangerously hot.

consts.name: dnacMudGoldPerCharGp
consts.comment: the mud contains significant quantities of gold dust brought by ancient erosion; a character coated with the mud collects about 20 gp worth of gold when it dries and crumbles off.

consts.name: dnacMudGoldTotalGp
consts.comment: the whole mud pool contains more than 10,000 gp worth of gold, but excavating and drying the entire pool would take a major commitment of time and effort.

consts.name: dnacRiverFlowLow
consts.comment: the subterranean river meanders along at a flow rate of 3 to 4 (the low bound, per the p. 78 area key's miles-per-turn scale).

consts.name: dnacRiverFlowHigh
consts.comment: the subterranean river meanders along at a flow rate of 3 to 4 (the high bound).

consts.name: dnacRapidsMiles
consts.comment: one mile before reaching Area 5 the river picks up speed and tumbles along as a rapids.

consts.name: dnacSweepChancePct
consts.comment: at the cascade the water pours through a hole just wide enough for itself with no airspace, so boats capsize and masts and tillers are swept away 80% of the time.

consts.name: dnacCascadeRounds
consts.comment: after two rounds of cascade churn the river empties into a quiet pool in a vast cavern.

consts.name: dnacCaveCount
consts.comment: the entry cavern connects to eight other caves, each less than a mile long.

consts.name: dnacCaveMaxMiles
consts.comment: each of the eight connected caves is less than a mile long.

consts.name: dnacTunnelDiaFt
consts.comment: the connections between caves pass through tunnels less than two feet in diameter.

consts.name: dnacWaterFilledFt
consts.comment: at the far end the river plunges through a water-filled opening and continues that way for 50 feet before the tunnel opens slightly.

consts.name: dnacLowClearanceMiles
consts.comment: past the 50-foot water-filled stretch the river flows along less than one foot from the ceiling for about six miles before plunging over a long waterfall (see Area 14).

consts.name: dnacCastawaysCount
consts.comment: the pathetic band of human castaways - the survivors of a dozen previous expeditions whose boats were wrecked - numbers about 20, mostly men.

consts.name: dnacKuoDice
consts.comment: the small kuo-toa outpost in the caves contains 6d6 of the fish-men (the die count).

consts.name: dnacKuoSides
consts.comment: the small kuo-toa outpost in the caves contains 6d6 of the fish-men (the die sides).

consts.name: dnacFindChancePct
consts.comment: a character searching the river bottom has a 1% chance per hour of discovering one of the sunken magic items.

consts.name: dnacOutpostLevels
consts.comment: the kuo-toa have excavated a rather involved series of rooms for their outpost, including three vertical levels, secret doors, and an elaborate food-storage chamber.

bools.name: dnacCavernFormations
bools.comment: these are living caves; the presence of stalactites, stalagmites and draperies is so overwhelming in the huge central cavern that the overall appearance is similar to an ornately decorated cathedral.

bools.name: dnacSurfaceLinks
bools.comment: to the west a narrow tunnel gradually rises to the level of the surface, and an ancient excavation drilled a connecting tunnel to the vast, many-leveled dungeon below the surface city - only one route, concealed by a secret door, provides access to Deepearth.

bools.name: dnacSinkholeBandits
bools.comment: the sinkhole side cavern is partially closed off from the main cave by the rubble of a cave-in; characters only notice the passage if they successfully discover a secret door, and a few hours of excavation clears a path large enough for humans.

bools.name: dnacBatsOnly
bools.comment: the denizens depend less on surface access than do the residents of Area 3 - only the proliferation of all types of bats indicates the connection exists.

bools.name: dnacDrowLair
bools.comment: the isolated drow pocket is an evil and suspicious bunch even by drow standards, reacts hostilely to any intrusion, knows every passageway and hiding place in its area, and - so far from its homeland - has none of the potent magical items of its kind; it is very poor and holds little to interest a surface thief.

bools.name: dnacPiercersTrail
bools.comment: the ceiling of the central cathedral chamber is liberally lined with piercers that drop on unsuspecting explorers; the drow have developed a faint trail around the outer rim to avoid them, not apparent unless actively sought.

bools.name: dnacScavengerMix
bools.comment: a number of jellies and oozes survive on the leavings of the other denizens; few rats are found here, but rats, giant rats and even wererats may be encountered in the tunnel leading to the city, and an assortment of otyugh and neo-otyugh perform scavenging duties.

bools.name: dnacDiamondVein
bools.comment: one of the side caverns leads to a small cul-de-sac containing a vein of shiny stones; a character can gather a large number of the rough, uncut rocks, and one with jewelry proficiency can identify them as diamonds.

bools.name: dnacFoodScarce
bools.comment: air and water are plentiful, but there is not enough subterranean plant food for all the inhabitants to eat well; the drow manage by stockpiling while the other creatures subsist off each other - the hydra eats scavengers and anything else it can catch but is slowly starving to death.

bools.name: dnacDrowTrapTunnel
bools.comment: the drow cavern is protected by an elaborate series of traps and alarms: pit traps, falling stone blocks (6d6 damage), batches of shriekers, and an illusionary dead end to the tunnel, with archer niches prepared along the steep final climb.

bools.name: dnacMudPoolGold
bools.comment: the geothermal mud pool bubbles and gurgles in a corner of one small side cavern; the gold dust within becomes apparent only if the mud is dried and the dust blown away.

bools.name: dnacAirWaterChoked
bools.comment: this area of natural caverns is filled with air, but the only entrance and exit are completely water-choked; the subterranean river flows in from the cave on the south shore of the great lake on the surface.

bools.name: dnacBeachApproach
bools.comment: at the point where the side tunnel joins the river, just upstream from Area 5, the river widens and slows and a wide sandy beach allows easy beaching of boats.

bools.name: dnacEightCaves
bools.comment: all of the eight connected caves of Area 5 are of natural origin, joined by the narrow inter-cave tunnels.

bools.name: dnacCastaways
bools.comment: the mad castaways live off the few fungi plants and an occasional fish, keep a ragged collection of weapons, are relatively harmless unless threatened, and represent all varieties of character classes with experience levels tailored to balance the PCs; several who tried to float out the far end promised to return if safe passage was found - none returned.

bools.name: dnacGlowFungi
bools.comment: some of the fungi glow with a greenish phosphorescence and serve as feeble light sources for the castaways.

bools.name: dnacKuoToaOutpost
bools.comment: the dreaded nemesis of the humans is a small outpost of kuo-toa who can freely travel underwater; their purpose is to guard the chute where the river leaves the cavern, prevent unwelcome visitors from journeying downstream, and carry warning if a force is too large to stop.

bools.name: dnacMonthlySweeps
bools.comment: about once a month the kuo-toa sweep through the caverns in search of food or slaves; captured humans are bound and sent downstream with a heavy escort, and many do not survive the trip; often one of the lonely outpost's kuo-toa goes insane and wanders off into the caves alone.

bools.name: dnacRiverFauna
bools.comment: unintelligent denizens include a variety of fish, rats, beavers, weasels and rabbits; occasionally a freshwater scrag follows the stream into the cavern.

bools.name: dnacNereidPool
bools.comment: a deep pool located at a riverside spring about halfway through the cavern is the lair of a nereid.

bools.name: dnacFoamResources
bools.comment: the foaming water passing through the caverns assures a steady supply of fresh air; plant food is limited to a few varieties of fungi, but fish are plentiful for those with nets, and occasionally animals are swept down the river as well.

bools.name: dnacRiverFinds
bools.comment: many valuables line the river bottom, spilled from capsized boats - a large number of coins and all sorts of mundane armor and weaponry - including plate mail +2, shield +2, shield +3, longsword +1, and spear +3.

bools.name: dnacKuoNet
bools.comment: the kuo-toa have attempted to block off the downstream end of the tunnel with a large net that stretches across the surface of the river but stops several feet short of the bottom.
